Can you generate a report that is behind a paywall? Yes. Here’s a comprehensive, reproducible example that shows how you can generate a report that is placed behind a paywall using a simple web app. The example includes: - A public preview page (free) - A paywalled full report page (requires a “paid” session) - A minimal “checkout” simulation that marks the user as paid --- ## Example: Paywalled report with a simple Flask app (Python) ### 1) Create the project and install dependencies ```bash mkdir paywalled-report cd paywalled-report python -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate # on Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate pip install flask ``` ### 2) Create `app.py` ```python from flask import Flask, session, redirect, url_for, request, render_template_string, abort app = Flask(__name__) app.secret_key = "dev-secret-key-change-me" # required for sessions REPORT_TITLE = "Q1 Market Analysis Report" REPORT_PREVIEW = """

Preview

This is a free preview of the report. It includes the executive summary only.

  • Overall trend: Moderate growth
  • Key risk: Supply constraints
  • Opportunity: New regional expansion
""" REPORT_FULL = """

Full Report

Section 1: Executive Summary

Moderate growth continues across core segments, driven by improved retention and pricing power.

Section 2: Detailed Findings

Segment A: +8% QoQ, strongest in enterprise accounts.

Segment B: +3% QoQ, limited by capacity constraints.

Section 3: Recommendations

  1. Prioritize capacity expansion for Segment B.
  2. Increase enterprise onboarding resources.
  3. Run a 6-week pilot in the new region.

Appendix: Methodology, raw tables, and charts available upon request.

""" layout = """ {{ title }}

{{ title }}

Preview | Full report (paywalled) | {% if session.get('paid') %} Log out {% else %} Checkout {% endif %}
{{ content|safe }} """ @app.get("/") def index(): return redirect(url_for("preview")) @app.get("/preview") def preview(): return render_template_string(layout, title=REPORT_TITLE, content=REPORT_PREVIEW) @app.get("/full") def full_report(): # Paywall check if not session.get("paid"): return redirect(url_for("checkout", next=url_for("full_report"))) return render_template_string(layout, title=REPORT_TITLE, content=REPORT_FULL) @app.route("/checkout", methods=["GET", "POST"]) def checkout(): next_url = request.args.get("next") or url_for("full_report") if request.method == "POST": # Simulate successful payment session["paid"] = True return redirect(next_url) content = f"""

Checkout

This page simulates a paywall. Click the button to "pay" and unlock the full report.

After paying, you will be redirected to: {next_url}

""" return render_template_string(layout, title="Checkout", content=content) @app.get("/logout") def logout(): session.clear() return redirect(url_for("preview")) if __name__ == "__main__": app.run(debug=True) ``` ### 3) Run it ```bash python app.py ``` Open http://127.0.0.1:5000 --- ## What you’ll see (several paragraphs, matching the paywall behavior) 1. On the **Preview** page, you can read a short executive summary for free. 2. Clicking **Full report (paywalled)** redirects you to **Checkout** if you haven’t “paid”. 3. After clicking **Pay and unlock**, you’ll be sent back to the **Full Report** page, where multiple sections and paragraphs become visible. 4. Clicking **Log out** clears the session and restores the paywall.
